title: In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/substrate-gap.ts, make exactly ONE edit: replace the following FIVE consecutiv
description:
In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/substrate-gap.ts, make exactly ONE edit: replace the following FIVE consecutive lines with the FIVE lines given below. Only the FOURTH line changes.

REPLACE these five consecutive lines, verbatim:
      const proc = unitAlreadyBusy
        ? null
        : Bun.spawnSync(["systemctl", "start", "--no-block", "gap-compose.service"], { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
      if (proc?.exitCode !== 0) {
        console.error(`[substrate-gap] gap-compose failed to start (systemctl exit ${proc?.exitCode ?? 'unknown'})`);

WITH these five lines, verbatim:
      const proc = unitAlreadyBusy
        ? null
        : Bun.spawnSync(["systemctl", "start", "--no-block", "gap-compose.service"], { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
      if (proc !== null && proc.exitCode !== 0) {
        console.error(`[substrate-gap] gap-compose failed to start (systemctl exit ${proc?.exitCode ?? 'unknown'})`);

Lines 1, 2, 3 and 5 are unchanged and must be reproduced exactly. The only difference is that the condition `if (proc?.exitCode !== 0) {` becomes `if (proc !== null && proc.exitCode !== 0) {`.

CRITICAL ANCHORING NOTE: the line `if (proc?.exitCode !== 0) {` appears TWICE in this file, in two duplicated blocks. You must change ONLY the FIRST occurrence — the one immediately following the Bun.spawnSync line shown above. That is why the anchor above includes the spawnSync line, which is unique. Do NOT change the second occurrence, which appears roughly ten lines further down. Do not delete or otherwise modify the second block in this change.

WHY THE CURRENT CONDITION IS WRONG. A few lines above, `proc` is deliberately set to null when the `unitAlreadyBusy` guard decides a compose is already in flight and the spawn should be SKIPPED. That is the correct, intended, successful path. But `proc?.exitCode` on a null `proc` evaluates to `undefined`, and `undefined !== 0` is TRUE, so the error branch fires and logs 'gap-compose failed to start (systemctl exit unknown)'. The guard working exactly as designed is therefore reported as a failure to start.

MEASURED, 2026-09-11 12:46:36. Three consecutive journal lines from this vessel:
  [substrate-gap] gap-compose unit NOT started for recommit-route-edit-79343a78-narrowed-typecheck_dangling_reference — a compose is already in flight
  [substrate-gap] gap-compose failed to start (systemctl exit unknown)
  [substrate-gap] gap-compose failed to start (systemctl exit unknown)
The first line announces the deliberate skip; the next two announce it as a failure. Nothing failed.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND NOISE. This exact message was, until an hour ago, also the signature of a genuine deadlock in which a synchronous systemctl call never returned. One message string is now emitted for two completely different states — 'the guard correctly skipped the spawn' and 'the spawn genuinely failed' — which makes the log unable to distinguish a healthy suppression from a real fault. A diagnostic that cannot discriminate between success and failure is worse than no diagnostic, because it is trusted.

The corrected condition leaves the genuine-failure path completely intact: when the spawn DID run and returned a non-zero exit code, `proc` is non-null and `proc.exitCode !== 0` is true, so the error still logs exactly as before. The only behaviour that changes is that a deliberately-skipped spawn stops being announced as a failure. Note also that `proc.exitCode` is now accessed without the optional-chaining `?.` because the null case is already excluded by the left-hand side of the `&&`.

All identifiers are already in scope: proc, unitAlreadyBusy. This cannot change any type.
